 Oral Judgment
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)

This appeal is filed by the injured seeking for enhancement of the compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 05.12.2018 passed in MVC No.511/2017 by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Jamkhandi1.
2.

Learned counsel Sri. Siddappa Sajjan appearing for the appellant/injured vehemently contends that the Tribunal has erred in assessing income of the injured at Rs.7,000/- per month which is on the lower side and committed an error in assessing the disability at 15% to the whole body, which is also on the lower side and contrary to the oral testimony of PW2- Doctor and other medical evidence on record.

He also submits that the award of compensation under other heads is also on 'Tribunal',
for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:13046-DB the lower side, hence, seeks enhancement of the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Preeti Shashank appearing for the respondent/Insurer supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that taking note of pleadings and evidence, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under all heads, which needs no interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, she seeks dismissal of appeal.
4. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 5. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 13.05.2017, the appellant sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
On filing of claim petition by the injured, the Tribunal has partly allowed the same by awarding total compensation of Rs.5,25,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
We are of the considered view that the Tribunal has committed grave error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.7,000/- per month.

The accident is of the year 2017, hence, we NC:
2024:KHC-D:13046-DB notionally re-assess the income of the injured at Rs.10,250/- per month placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
6. The Tribunal considering the oral testimony of PW2 and other medical evidence on record has assessed the disability of the injured at 15%.

We have perused Wound Certificate at Ex.P6,
Discharge Summary at Exs.P15 and P16 and Disability Certificate at Ex.P17.
The evidence on record indicate that the injured was treated at Sanjivini Hospital, Bijapur initially and later at KLE Hospital, Belagavi where he was operated.

The medical evidence on record indicates that there is a shortening of left lower limb with restriction of movement, malunited fracture of left femure and also malunited fracture of right tibia fibula.
Implants were inserted after performing the surgery.
PW2-Doctor has assessed disability at 53% to the left lower limb, 38% to the right lower limb and 15% to the left upper limb.
We are of the view that the assessment of disability by PW2 is without any proper reasoning and basis.

Though PW2 has initially treated the injured, but actual operation was performed on the injured at KLE Hospital, Belagavi, hence, PW2 cannot be considered as a NC:
2024:KHC-D:13046-DB treated Doctor to the injured for the entire duration of treatment.

Considering the nature of fractures, more particularly the fracture is malunited, we are of the considered view that the interest of justice would be met if we re-assess the disability at 35% for the purpose of determination of compensation.
7. There is no dispute with regard to the application of multiplier of 17.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of future earnings due to disability as under:
Rs.10,250 x 12 x 17 x 35/100 = Rs.7,31,850/-
8.
The evidence on record indicates that the appellant was inpatient for a period of more than five months and has undergone four operations.

The evidence on record indicates that the appellant was initially provided treatement at Dr.G.N.Sanadi Hospital, Jamkhandi, then in Sanjivini Hospital,
Bijapur later he was shifted to Dr.Sanjeev Kulkarni Hospital, Miraj and thereafter he was referred to KLE Hospital, Belagavi for further treatment.
Considering the same we re
- assess the compensation as under:

NC: 2024:KHC-D:13046-DB Pain and suffering Rs. 70,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs. 2,66,200/-

Future medical expenses Rs.10,000  Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 61,500/-
 Food, transport & attendant charges Rs. 30,000/-
 Loss of future earning Rs. 7,31,850/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
 ---------------

sentences.text:
9. In all, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.11,99,550/- as against Rs.5,25,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

10. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal stands partly allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.11,99,550/- as against Rs.5,25,400/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The respondent/insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from today.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:13046-DB e) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.
f) TCR be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.

g) Draw modified award accordingly.
h) No order as to costs.
Sd/-
(KRISHNA S.DIXIT) JUDGE Sd/-
